name: MA-period sweep

shape_findings.1M_dist: monotonic smooth rise from n=20 (-0.220) to n=200 (+0.096), crossing zero near n=100-110. No spike -- a genuine gradient, longer MA = less-bad distance signal at 1M.
shape_findings.1M_slope: monotonic rise from n=20 (-0.017) to a broad hump n=100-120 (0.164/0.168), dips at n=150 (0.127), then a single high point at n=200 (0.247). The n=200 point is the one place that looks like an isolated spike rather than part of the n=100-120 plateau -- flagged, not fully clean.
shape_findings.1Y_dist: monotonic smooth rise from n=20 (0.362) plateauing n=100-200 (0.776-0.800, essentially flat) -- clean broad plateau, longer MAs generically win, no single lucky length.
shape_findings.1Y_slope: genuine hump peaking at n=55-75 (0.692-0.720, with 65 at 0.717) then declining through n=100-200 (0.701 down to 0.587-0.605) -- a real, non-spike plateau CENTERED on the 55-75 band that Principal's 65DMA sits inside; this is the cleanest 'stable plateau not a lucky length' result in the sweep, and it directly supports 65 over 50 or 100+ for the SLOPE construct.

answer_to_principal: No isolated one-lucky-length spike anywhere except possibly 1M-slope's n=200 point. Two distinct regimes: (1) DISTANCE-from-MA wants LONGER windows generically (plateaus at 100-200d, both horizons), (2) SLOPE-of-MA at the 1Y horizon has a genuine hump centered on 55-75d -- 65 sits right in the middle of that plateau, which is the strongest evidence in this bucket that 65 (not 50, not 100+) is a structurally sound choice specifically for the momentum/slope construct.
harness_verdict: KILL (all 48 sub-cards) -- PBO>0.5 on every variant (0.85-1.00 range); most 1M variants also fail IC_IR>=0.20 and/or lag_test_delta<=0.25.
issue_flag: [DATA] DSR ~ 0 (1e-20 to 1e-70) on literally every H001/H002/H042 card. Root cause: trials_counter.json increments per evaluate() call keyed by family; running the full 12-length x 2-construct x 2-horizon sweep under family='H002' in one session drove n_trials up to 48 within that single family, which the harness's sigma_SR=1 Bailey-LdP deflation (FND_harness.md) punishes extremely harshly -- DSR collapses toward 0 regardless of the true signal quality. Likewise PBO>0.5 fired on EVERY one of the 62 cards run in this session (range 0.85-1.00), including cards with IC_IR>0.7 and clean lag tests, which is suspicious as a blanket result across an entire family rather than a differentiated per-factor read. This may be an honest reflection of a genuinely short/autocorrelated panel (only 61 monthly dates, ~36-48 valid for 1Y) rather than a harness bug -- not diagnosed further here (out of scope: this worker does not touch harness.py). Flagging for Dr. Sameer Bhat / the prioritizer: (a) whether bulk single-session parameter sweeps should be split into separate low-n families before scoring, since one big family sweep structurally guarantees DSR~0 and possibly inflates PBO gate failures too, and (b) whether PBO firing on 100% of 62 runs this session (vs the harness's own demo card which was 0.97, also a KILL) suggests the CSCV single-factor adaptation over-flags PBO for smooth/autocorrelated trend factors on this panel length.
